sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Oklahoma, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Monday, October 19Passed

Your request had to reach your County Election Board by 5 p.m. on the third Monday (15 days) before the election: Monday, October 19, 2026. That deadline has passed. Voters who become physically incapacitated after that time, and first responders, emergency workers or military voters deployed after it, may be able to ask for an emergency absentee ballot from their County Election Board. (official page)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

A ballot sent by U.S. mail or a delivery company must be received by your County Election Board by 7 p.m. on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026. A ballot you hand deliver must be turned in by the end of business hours on the day before the election, Monday, November 2, 2026. A postmark is not enough. (official page)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Saturday, October 31, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Ask for a ballot online, on Oklahoma’s own site

At school away from home, in Oklahoma or in another state? What Oklahoma says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

No reason is needed. Any registered voter in Oklahoma may vote by absentee ballot (the "standard" absentee ballot). Some voters, such as those who are physically incapacitated, blind or in a nursing home, can use other kinds of absentee ballots with their own rules. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • Online. Apply on the OK Voter Portal. By state law, any application must give an ID number that matches the one on your voter registration record. You can ask for a ballot for one election, several, or every election in the calendar year. Open it (official page)
  • By mail. Print the application form, or ask your County Election Board to mail you one at any address, and send it to your County Election Board by mail, fax or email. Open it (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail it to your County Election Board (first-class postage needed), or send it by a delivery service with tracking such as FedEx or UPS. It must arrive by 7 p.m. on Election Day. The state suggests mailing at least a week ahead. (official page)
  • In person. Hand deliver it to your County Election Board yourself by the end of business on Monday, November 2, 2026, and show the same proof of identity needed to vote in person. You must return your own ballot: returning another voter's standard absentee ballot is against the law. The state's pages do not describe drop boxes. (official page)

What the envelope needs

The signed statement (affidavit) on the yellow envelope of a standard absentee ballot must be notarized, whether you mail it or hand deliver it. Many banks, credit unions, libraries and other businesses notarize absentee ballots for free, and Oklahoma notaries may not charge for it. Ballots for voters who are physically incapacitated or blind instead need two witnesses. (official page)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on Oklahoma’s own site (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Wednesday, October 28, 2026 to Saturday, October 31, 2026.

Anyone can vote early in person, no reason needed, in the county where you are registered: Wednesday, October 28, Thursday, October 29 and Friday, October 30, 2026, 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., and Saturday, October 31, 2026, 8 a.m. to 2 p.m. (The rule: Wednesday before a General Election, Thursday and Friday before any election, and the Saturday before.) (official page)

Students

At school in Oklahoma, away from home

Oklahoma law says you register at your address of residence. The state's own example: a student registered in Tulsa who goes to college in Norman can ask for an absentee ballot mailed to Norman, or can register to vote in Norman instead. Registering in Norman cancels the Tulsa registration. For November 3, 2026, the deadline to ask for a standard absentee ballot (5 p.m. Monday, October 19) has passed. (official page)

At school in another state, with Oklahoma as home

The state's pages do not speak to students out of state separately. Its general rule: you register at your address of residence; any registered voter can get a standard absentee ballot without a reason; the County Election Board can mail an application to any address; and the ballot's signed statement must be notarized. (official page)

Military and overseas

Uniformed services members, their spouses and dependents, and U.S. citizens living outside the country can apply on the OK Voter Portal, by mail, fax or email, or with the federal FPCA, by 5 p.m. on October 19, 2026 (15 days before; that deadline has passed). You can ask to get the ballot electronically, which the state recommends. Voted ballots can be returned by mail, a delivery service, or fax, and must be received by 7 p.m. on Election Day, November 3, 2026, with a signed and dated statement. A military voter deployed after the request deadline can ask for an emergency absentee ballot. The federal write-in ballot (FWAB) is a backup. (official page)

Oklahoma in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • The deadline to ask for a standard absentee ballot for November 3, 2026 passed on October 19. Early voting (October 28 to 31) and Election Day are still ahead.
  • Oklahoma requires a notary on a standard absentee ballot's envelope. Plan for this before mailing your ballot back.
  • The state warns that absentee ballot laws can change and that any changes will be explained in your ballot packet.

How this was checked

  • The Federal Voting Assistance Program page loads by script and could not be read; it is linked, not quoted.
